New handloom, skilling and UPTEX Mitra initiatives, plus an AI-readiness study, were unveiled for industry sourcing teams.

title: Bangladesh curbs bonded cotton yarn imports as BGMEA, BKMEA protest
summary:
Bangladesh's National Board of Revenue has suspended duty-free bonded imports of 10-30 count cotton yarn, while allowing shipments against bank guarantees.
Exporters must secure release of guarantees after proceeds are repatriated, with certificates from BGMEA, BKMEA or BTMA.
BGMEA and BKMEA say the move raises financing pressure and could disrupt apparel exports and buyer confidence.

title: India’s new cotton arrives as US-China dryness supports prices
summary:
New-season cotton arrivals have begun in northern India ahead of the October 1 season, led by Haryana and Rajasthan, with around 1,400-1,450 bales reported.
Dry weather concerns in the US and China are supporting ICE cotton futures and Indian prices despite fresh supplies.
Kapas prices are at or above MSP, limiting early CCI buying and giving private ginners more room.

title: China's foreign exchange reserves rise 0.57% to $3.44 trn in Aug
summary:
China’s foreign exchange reserves rose by $19.5 billion, or 0.57 per cent, from July to $3.4383 trillion at end-August 2026.
For textile and apparel exporters, importers and sourcing teams, the reading is a macro signal to track with China’s trade and export data.
Currency translation and asset price changes led the increase; Wen Bin linked it to dollar weakness and expected resilient exports.

title: Netherlands' $769 mn RRF request gets EU Commission backing
summary:
European Commission backed the Netherlands’ fourth RRF request, advancing €661 million (~$769 million) tied to nine milestones and 15 targets.
Funds cover renewables, efficiency upgrades, green hydrogen, digital education and reskilling, signalling clean and skills investment.
EFC has four weeks to opine; payment follows a Commission decision, with final RRF requests due by end-September 2026.

title: China's 5.80% FDY jump raises a new cost risk for buyers
summary:
Chinese FDY benchmarks saw their sharpest intra-week rally in weeks between August 31 and September 4, 2026, TexPro data showed.
FDY 150D/96F rose 5.80 per cent, FDY 75D/36F 4.79 per cent and FDY 100D/72F 3.24 per cent in domestic China.
The move was cost-driven after Brent crude gained nearly 9 per cent and MEG hit its daily trading limit, while buying interest stayed cautious.

title: India’s DGFT rolls out secure API integration for export certificates
summary:
India’s DGFT has introduced an Open API facility for issuing and verifying Certificates of Origin through the Trade Connect e-Platform.
Eligible exporters can link ERP, accounting or business software with the CoO system to reduce duplicate entry, errors and processing time.
The facility covers preferential and non-preferential CoOs, supporting tariff-claim and customs documentation workflows.

title: Pakistan's +5.69% modal shock could reprice its MMF supply chain
summary:
Pakistan’s modal fibre rose 5.69 per cent to PKR 836/kg on September 1; China and India fibre and Indian MMCF yarn stayed flat.
Higher RLNG, LPG, freight and cellulosic costs, not currency, tax or cotton substitution, are cited as the stronger driver.
Pakistani MMCF-blend spinners face margin or pass-through pressure, and EU and US buyers may see quote revisions within one to two order cycles.

title: SCB, UKEF discuss Bangladesh trade corridor, export diversification
summary:
Standard Chartered Bangladesh and UK Export Finance discussed strengthening the Bangladesh trade corridor and supporting export diversification at a Dhaka roundtable. 
The talks focused on UKEF-backed financing, export credit facilities and project pipelines covering infrastructure, sustainability and industrial upgrading, with participation from businesses in various sectors.

title: Bangladesh, US review trade & investment conditions
summary:
US envoy Brent T Christensen told Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir that US companies are keen to operate in Bangladesh.
The talks covered investment, bilateral trade, energy co-operation, import policy changes and transparency in large infrastructure projects.
For sourcing teams, the discussion points to continued focus on market access, energy supply and business-process reform.

title: US' Lands' End returns to profit as Q2 revenue rises to $302 mn
summary:
Lands' End returned to Q2 FY26 profit, with net income of $3.5 million as revenue rose 2.7 per cent to $302.0 million.
US e-commerce led growth, rising 9.0 per cent to $182.4 million; Outfitters gained, while third-party sales dropped 20.4 per cent.
Lands' End reaffirmed FY26 guidance, with inventory up 13 per cent for seasonal build as operations normalised before the holiday season.

title: US apparel imports are weak; so why did bookings jump 79%?
summary:
US HS61–62 apparel imports fell 7.77 per cent to $36.90 billion in H1 2026, but the contraction narrowed from 11.82 per cent in Q1 to 3.28 per cent in Q2.
Clothing and accessories-store sales rose 5.9 per cent to $151.09 billion; June's inventory-to-sales ratio fell to 2.14.
US-bound HS61–62 ocean bookings reached 21,434 TEU in June, up 79 per cent, led by Vietnam and Cambodia.

title: Australia’s apparel imports dip 7.5% in July 2026
summary:
Australia’s apparel imports fell 7.57 per cent to Au$1.025 billion in July 2026; textile yarn, fabrics and made-up imports eased 2.58 per cent.
Fibre imports edged up to Au$12 million, while textile fibre exports declined 9.92 per cent to Au$629 million, Australian Bureau of Statistics data showed.
Fiscal 2025–26 saw apparel imports down 4.60 per cent and fibre exports up 7.72 per cent.

title: Bangladesh’s RMG sector bets on technology for a productivity edge
summary:
Bangladesh apparel exporters are adopting digital monitoring, data-driven production and AI tools to raise productivity, reduce downtime and improve quality.
Some factories report gains of up to 25 per cent versus manual monitoring, though results vary by technology, conditions and measurement.
The shift also raises concerns over worker pressure, privacy and fair sharing of productivity gains.

title: Jordan’s clothing exports rise 1.8% to $1.19 bn in H1 2026
summary:
Jordan’s apparel and clothing accessory exports rose 1.8 per cent year on year to JOD 846.6 million (~$1.19 billion) in H1 2026.
Knitted apparel grew 3.0 per cent to JOD 830.7 million and made up more than 98 per cent of clothing exports.
Woven apparel exports fell 36.4 per cent, while knitted and woven apparel imports rose 2.4 per cent in H1.

title: RMG exports from B’desh in green zone as shipment jumps in August 2026
summary:
Bangladesh's RMG exports rose 5.12 per cent to $7.495 billion in July-August 2026, backed by a strong August, EPB provisional data show. 
Knitwear grew 6.17 per cent to $4.193 billion, while woven apparel increased 3.81 per cent to $3.301 billion. 
Home textile exports gained 11.17 per cent to $154.55 million, but cotton and cotton products fell 13.02 per cent to $82.24 million.

title: As Sri Lanka’s exports grow, is apparel losing momentum?
summary:
Sri Lanka’s combined merchandise and services exports reached $10.49 billion in January–July 2026, up 5.48 per cent year-on-year. 
Apparel and textiles fell 6.50 per cent to $2.88 billion, diverging from broader export growth. 
July apparel and textile exports dropped 8.8 per cent to $437.59 million, with shipments declining across the United States, European Union and United Kingdom.

title: A meeting that highlights the fraying edges of Bangladesh’s RMG story
summary:
BGMEA told the President that nearly 400 garment factories have closed in Bangladesh over three years, as production costs rose almost 40 per cent. 
Inadequate gas supplies, higher energy tariffs, wages and bank interest rates are forcing many factories to operate below half capacity. 
Garment exports contracted 1.64 per cent in FY2025-26 and fell 1.92 per cent in July of FY2026-27.

title: US' PVH Corp Q2 FY26 revenue hits $2.1 bn, profit tops estimate
summary:
PVH’s Q2 FY26 revenue fell 3 per cent to $2.10 billion, but non-GAAP EPS of $3.70 beat guidance as gross margin reached 63.0 per cent.
DTC gains in the Americas and APAC, e-commerce growth and tariff refunds offset weaker wholesale, licensing declines and EMEA pressure.
The Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger owner reaffirmed FY26 guidance, with Q3 revenue seen down low single digits YoY.
